## Failures

### `exploration_is_not_growing`

policy entropy went -0.66 -> -0.55 (+0.12). A policy that is learning gets more decisive; rising entropy means the entropy bonus is beating the policy gradient, which on a Gaussian policy it will do indefinitely because entropy is unbounded above.

### `the_off_track_rate_came_down`

episodes ending off the road went nan -> 1.00. A rate stuck at 1.00 means every episode is a crash and the policy has never seen the behaviour it is supposed to be reinforcing.

### `the_deployed_policy_completes_the_task`

the mean-action policy — the one you would ship — finishes 0% of laps and covers 92 m. Sampling its actions instead gives 0% and 87 m. **The deployed number is the result.** A run whose sampled policy performs well and whose mean action does not has not produced a driver; it has produced a policy whose competence lives in its own exploration noise, and the sampled figure describes something you cannot ship.

### `the_policy_stayed_inside_the_tire_model`

the deployed policy's worst slip angle reached 15.8 deg against our 12 deg bound, with 11.3% of steps beyond it (sampled, for comparison: 22.7 deg, 5.2% of steps — training-time only). Every minimum-time solve in Seasons 1 and 2 constrains this; the environment deliberately does not, so the policy is free to operate where the Magic Formula is extrapolating and the forces are arithmetic rather than measurement.

### `the_tire_file_s_own_load_range_was_respected`

11.0% of the deployed policy's steps left the tire file's own declared operating range (sampled: 5.1%). That bound is the file's, not ours, and outside it the model is not extrapolating from a fit — it has no fit.

## Technical notes

*Recorded, never pass/fail. These are where the model is correct but a reference is not, or where a number is worth watching.*

### the_two_action_dimensions_need_different_exploration

Steering rate and throttle have useful scales an order of magnitude apart — 0.037 of authority against the whole [-1, 1] interval — so a single exploration standard deviation cannot serve both. With one value small enough for the steering, the policy never sampled braking at all and sat at full throttle for half a million steps. This run uses [0.082, 0.368].
